topic: cubit registered as singleton
right: getIt..registerFactory(() => ArchiveCubit(repo: getIt()));
wrong: getIt..registerLazySingleton(() => ArchiveCubit(repo: getIt()));
why: A singleton cubit keeps the previous screen's state and emits after close(). Cubits are always registerFactory.

topic: easy_localization shadows dart:ui TextDirection
why: easy_localization re-exports package:intl, whose TextDirection is a class with LTR/RTL constants - not the dart:ui enum with .ltr/.rtl that Text.textDirection takes. Any widget file that both imports easy_localization and pins text direction (needed whenever English words sit in an Arabic-first UI) fails to compile until intl's version is hidden.

topic: cubit with several repos: named initializing formals, public fields
why: Dart forbids named parameters that start with an underscore, so `required this._progressRepo` will not compile and the private-field + initializer-list form trips prefer_initializing_formals. For a single dependency keep the house positional form `Cubit(this._repo)`; once there are two or more, name them and make the fields public - which also matches the golden ArchiveCubit pattern where the repo field is public and injectable in tests.

topic: presentation-only features legitimately have no data/ folder (R12)
why: R12 flags a missing data/ folder as a warning, not an error, precisely because it cannot tell an incomplete feature from a presentation-only one. When several screens read the same tables, one data-owning feature plus injected repos keeps `fromJson`/error mapping in a single place; duplicating a data layer per screen is the actual violation. Confirm and move on rather than scaffolding empty folders.

topic: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch on a Row inside a vertical ListView
why: In a vertical ListView every child is laid out with maxHeight: infinity. RenderFlex with CrossAxisAlignment.stretch passes BoxConstraints.tightFor(height: constraints.maxHeight) to each child, so the children get a tight infinite height and layout throws; the subtree is then left unsized and the next pointer event fails with "Cannot hit test a render box with no size". IntrinsicHeight resolves the row to the tallest child's intrinsic height first, which keeps the equal-height look that stretch was there for (needed because translated labels wrap to two lines in Arabic but one in English). This is the same family as the house rule "never Expanded in an unconstrained scrollable" — stretch on the cross axis is the vertical twin of it. flutter analyze cannot catch this: it is a layout-time error only.

topic: R10 fires on Expanded and SingleChildScrollView in exclusive branches
wrong:
// "Fixing" an R10 warning by removing a correct Expanded, or by wrapping the
// bounded Row in a SizedBox with a guessed height.
why: The real rule is that Expanded must not be a direct child of an unbounded scrollable. A Row's Expanded constrains width, which is bounded by the parent Column, so it is always safe; and a scroll view nested inside an Expanded is the standard way to give a scrollable bounded space. Checking the actual parent chain takes a moment and saves breaking working layout. Contrast with the genuine violation recorded for CrossAxisAlignment.stretch on a Row inside a vertical ListView, which flutter_check does not catch at all.

topic: stretch Row inside a scrollable needs IntrinsicHeight
why: On a Row, CrossAxisAlignment.stretch is vertical: the Row hands each child a tight height equal to its own. A direct child of a vertical ListView (or any scrollable) gets maxHeight: infinity, so there is no finite height to stretch to and the children are never laid out. IntrinsicHeight bounds the Row to the tallest child's intrinsic height, which both fixes the crash and keeps the equal-height cards that stretch was there for. Note this is a latent crash: it only fires once the screen's cubit reaches success and actually renders the row, so a screen stuck on an error or skeleton state hides it. In this project the same three-stat row exists in home, profile and progress; home had the IntrinsicHeight and the other two did not. When fixing one, grep `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` across lib/ and check every hit whose parent is a Row (Column + stretch is horizontal and safe inside a bounded-width parent).

topic: create or replace view only accepts columns appended last
right:
-- Start from the LATEST definition of the view (0005, not 0001) and append:
create or replace view public.word_overview
with (security_invoker = on) as
select
  ...                                   -- every existing column, same order
  (f.word_id is not null) as is_favorite,
  coalesce((select array_agg(i.list_id ...)), '{}'::text[]) as list_ids,
  w.field_id,                           -- new columns go last
  fl.name_en as field_name_en,
  fl.color   as field_color
from public.words w
join public.categories c on c.id = w.category_id
left join public.fields fl on fl.id = w.field_id
...;

-- A dependent view that used `w.*` expanded it at definition time, so it does
-- NOT inherit the new columns: replace it too, with the same body.
create or replace view public.word_list_entries ... select i.list_id, w.* ...;
wrong:
-- Re-stating word_overview from 0001 and slotting the new column in where it
-- belongs logically. Two separate failures:
create or replace view public.word_overview as
select
  w.id,
  w.category_id,
  w.field_id,            -- inserted mid-list -> 42P16 cannot change name of
  w.word,                --   view column "field_id" to "word"
  ...
  (f.word_id is not null) as is_favorite
  -- and `list_ids`, added by 0005, silently dropped -> the word-list chips
  --   stop rendering because WordModel.listIds is always empty
from public.words w ...
why: Postgres allows `create or replace view` to add trailing columns and nothing else — reordering, renaming or dropping one raises 42P16 on an applied database, and a column quietly left out breaks every client that reads it. Because each migration re-states the whole view, the one to copy from is the most recent migration that touched it, never 0001. Check which migrations redefine the view (`grep -l word_overview supabase/migrations/`) before writing a new one. The same applies to views built on it: `w.*` is expanded and frozen at creation, so a dependent view needs its own create-or-replace to pick the new columns up.

topic: RLS `to authenticated` on a table a pre-auth screen reads
wrong:
-- Copied from `categories_read` without checking WHO reads the table.
create policy fields_read on public.fields
  for select to authenticated using (true);

-- The field picker is a step on the REGISTER screen, so it runs as `anon`.
-- The anon role passes the policy and sees zero rows: the query SUCCEEDS,
-- so the UI shows its empty state ("no fields set up yet"), not its error
-- state. Nothing is logged and nothing is thrown.
why: Empty state vs error state is the diagnostic: an unapplied migration or a missing grant raises a PostgrestException that ErrorMapper turns into a failure state with a Retry button, while an RLS policy that excludes the caller returns an empty result set and renders the empty state instead. So "no rows, no error" on a freshly added table means the policy does not cover the role actually asking — check whether the screen runs before or after sign-in before copying a policy from another table. The second half matters just as much: a required form input backed by a list that can legitimately come back empty locks the user out of the screen entirely, so make it optional and enforce it somewhere a skip is possible. Same family as the skip guard on the choose-field redirect.

topic: scope a whole app by putting the filter in the view, not every query
why: A per-query filter is only as good as the next developer's memory, and it cannot cover views built on views: `word_list_entries` selects from `word_overview`, so a predicate inside `word_overview` reaches it for free while a client-side `.eq()` never would. Keeping the "no value = unrestricted" branch is what lets legacy rows and an un-set profile keep working instead of seeing an empty app. The cost is that the filter is invisible at the call site, so it must be stated in the view's comment AND the data source's class doc; leave any explicit `.eq(...)` that already exists in place, since it still helps the planner use the index and tells the reader what the query means.

topic: live notification refresh on a REST backend (no StreamBuilder)
why: StreamBuilder only applies to a backend that actually streams (Firestore/WebSocket). On a REST backend the live path is: push event -> broadcast bus -> cubit subscription -> silent re-fetch, which keeps the UI dumb and all refresh/loading/error behavior in the cubit. A registerLazySingleton cubit loading once in its constructor is the stale-data root cause: it needs push, app-resume, and screen-entry triggers. Silent background refreshes must preserve content, suppress error toasts, guard against duplicate in-flight requests, and re-apply optimistic reads that have not been confirmed by the backend yet.

topic: media player widgets inside a scrollable keep playing on scroll
why:
Any widget that owns a long-lived resource (VideoPlayerController, just_audio player, PdfViewerController, scroll/animation state) and sits as a child of a ListView/CustomScrollView MUST mix in AutomaticKeepAliveClientMixin, or scrolling it out of the cache extent silently destroys the resource and re-creates it — restarting playback and firing a duplicate network request (costly here: each re-create asks the API for a new expiring protected-media token).

Three details that make it work:
1. `super.build(context)` must be the first line of build(); the mixin dispatches its KeepAliveNotification from there and the keep-alive is a no-op without it.
2. The enclosing sliver needs `addAutomaticKeepAlives: true` — the default for ListView(children:) and ListView.builder, so nothing extra is needed there, but a hand-rolled SliverChildBuilderDelegate that disables it defeats the mixin.
3. Prefer `wantKeepAlive => true` over a conditional `=> _playback != null`: a conditional needs updateKeepAlive() when the resource changes, and calling it from a teardown reached via dispose() dispatches a notification on an element that is being unmounted. `State.mounted` is still true inside dispose(), so an `if (mounted)` guard does not protect against this.

Side effect to expect and design around: a kept-alive child that is offscreen is not rebuilt by the delegate, so prop changes (speed, a server position correction) reach it when it scrolls back into view, not immediately. Callbacks keep firing, because the State reads `widget.onTick` and that closure holds the stable cubit — so progress reporting continues while the player is scrolled away, which is the desired behavior.

Fixing this by hoisting the player out of the scrollable into a Column + Expanded(ListView) is a different product decision (a pinned/sticky player), not the minimal fix — don't change layout when the ask is only "don't stop playing".

topic: testing a CacheUtil-backed data source across several tests
why: `CacheUtil.init()` returns early when its static `_prefs` is already set (`if (_prefs != null) return;`), and the loaded SharedPreferences instance keeps its own in-memory copy of the values. Re-seeding with `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues` in a later test therefore changes nothing the instance reads — the second test silently sees values written by the first and the assertion fails on stale data. Note the prefix asymmetry too: mock initial values need the literal `flutter.` prefix (`'flutter.playback_speed'`), while CacheUtil/SharedPreferences calls take the bare key.

topic: TextDirection shadowed by easy_localization import
why: In any widget file that imports easy_localization, the bare name `TextDirection` resolves to intl's class (constants `TextDirection.LTR` / `.RTL`), not dart:ui's enum, so `TextDirection.ltr` fails with `undefined_getter`. Hiding it on the easy_localization import (or prefixing dart:ui) restores the Flutter enum. Separately, code-entry fields (OTP/PIN/phone/IBAN) must be wrapped in a `Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.ltr)` so digits fill left-to-right under the Arabic locale.

topic: per-item playback speed must be session-scoped, not persisted
why:
The user rejected the persisted, media-type-keyed design outright: "every lesson has its own speed", "it doesn't save locally after closing the app", "the default value is 1.0". Two separate mistakes were baked into the old code — scoping a per-item setting to a broad category (media type), and reaching for CacheUtil/SharedPreferences for state the user wants to expire with the process.

A data source still owns the store, so the architecture rule holds; "data source owns persistence" does not mean the store must be on disk. A static Map inside the data source is the right backing when the requirement is session-scoped: it outlives the per-lesson Cubit (so leaving the screen and returning keeps the choice) but dies with the process (so every lesson reopens at 1x).

Follow-through that is easy to miss: once the store is in memory the write is synchronous, so `Future<void> write(...)` becomes `void` and the Cubit's `setPlaybackSpeed` drops `async`/`await` — both call sites take it as `ValueChanged<PlaybackSpeed>`, which is satisfied either way. Also delete the now-dead CacheKeys entries (legacyPlaybackSpeed, audioPlaybackSpeed, videoPlaybackSpeed) and drop the redundant second read in loadLesson, whose comment about the route guessing the media type is false once the key is the lesson id.

Before scoping a player/viewer preference, ask what it belongs to — the item, the media kind, or the student — and whether it should outlive the process. Do not default to SharedPreferences.

topic: data model must not import presentation to reach an enum
why:
Dumb-UI layering runs one way: presentation may import data, data may never
import presentation. A model that reaches up into presentation/refactor/ inverts
it, and the breakage is not theoretical -- that model then cannot be used by a
data source or a local store without dragging a Flutter view file behind it, and
the feature stops being testable below the widget layer.

The tempting workarounds are both worse than moving the enum:
  * storing the step as `int stepIndex` -- inserting a step mid-enum silently
    re-keys every stored payload;
  * storing it as a bare `String` -- stringly typed, and every reader has to
    re-parse it.

The test for where an enum belongs is what it *is*, not where it was first
written: a vocabulary (which field, which step, which status) is data and
belongs in data/models/; how that vocabulary is *drawn* (which inputs a step
shows, labels, widths) is view data and stays in presentation/refactor/. Here
`RequestStep` was the vocabulary and only `RequestForm`'s grouping was view data,
so the enum moved and the grouping stayed.

Watch the extension when moving: Dart resolves an extension only if the library
declaring it is imported, so a consumer keeping the old import still sees the
enum type but loses `.isLast`/`.titleKey`, producing an undefined_getter error
at a line that looks untouched.

topic: terminal-state guard must precede a server capability flag
why: A visibility getter for a destructive action has two kinds of condition, and they are not symmetric. The terminal-state guard ("this record is closed") is a hard invariant and must be evaluated on its own; a server capability hint (`allowed_transitions`, `is_editable`) is only a permissive signal. Writing `flag || isOpen` lets the permissive signal satisfy the whole expression and defeat the invariant — a cancelled order whose payload still listed `cancelled` among its transitions got the cancel button back. Decide the fallback direction explicitly instead: guard the closed states absolutely, then choose whether an undocumented flag may hide the action. Here it may not — hiding a button the customer is entitled to press is unrecoverable in-app, while offering one the server refuses costs only a toast carrying the server's own reason, so the flag is deliberately not consulted and kept only for the day the transition names are documented. A widget test over one fixture per status (including a closed row with the flag set true) is what caught it; cover every status, not just the happy ones.

topic: faking wakelock_plus in tests
why: `WakelockPlus.toggle()` does not read `WakelockPlusPlatformInterface.instance` at call time. wakelock_plus/lib/wakelock_plus.dart holds a top-level `var wakelockPlusPlatformInstance = WakelockPlusPlatformInterface.instance;`, and Dart initialises top-level vars lazily on first access. So the very first `setUp` that assigns `.instance` happens to win (the lazy init captures that fake), and every later assignment is dead — the facade is permanently frozen to the first fake. Assigning `wakelockPlusPlatformInstance` (marked @visibleForTesting and exported from the package) is the only seam that re-points the facade per test. Same trap applies to any plugin that caches its platform in a top-level var rather than reading the registry per call.

topic: session termination keys off the API status code, never the account state
why: The dashboard owns the list of account states and adds to it without the app shipping. Any client-side enum of those strings is stale the moment an admin invents a state, and the failure mode is the dangerous direction: an unrecognised state reads as "not suspended", so a student the platform shut out keeps using the app. Status codes are a fixed contract — whichever state an account is moved into, the request comes back 401/403 — so keying off the code needs no code change when the state list grows, and the body is never parsed for wording (the old version matched Arabic substrings like 'موقوف' in messages, which breaks on any copy edit). Put the verdict in ErrorMapper and carry it on AppException so it is decided once; check it in BOTH the Dio interceptor and ApiClient, since an envelope API that answers 200 with a failure code never reaches an interceptor. Guard the sign-out on DeviceSessionService.hasSession so a refused login does not reset the stack under the login form. Trade-off to raise with the user first: if 403 also marks locked content in the app (it did here — lesson_detail, textbooks), making 403 session-ending logs students out of locked lessons, so either exclude those paths in the interceptor or confirm the user accepts it.

topic: cancel action affordance on in-progress download UI
why: An icon-only control with just a Tooltip is not a discoverable affordance on touch (no hover, tooltip never seen), and squeezed next to the byte ratio it reads as decoration on the progress row rather than as the action. The user's correction was "wanna the button to be more clear". Default to a labelled, full-width button for any cancel/stop on an in-progress operation, sized to the button it replaces so the card does not shift height when the state changes, themed through colorScheme.error (never hardcoded red), and built from the shared CustomOutlineButton instead of a per-feature InkWell. Keep the nullable callback gate (`if (onCancel != null)`) so operations that cannot be called off — e.g. preparing a preview link — simply show no button, and use isLoading for the winding-down state so a second tap cannot queue a second cancel.

topic: one EasyLocalization host per widget-test file
why: EasyLocalization keeps its loaded translations in a static. A second instance in the same isolate does not just render raw keys - its child subtree never builds at all, so finders return "Found 0 widgets" for widgets that are plainly in the pumpWidget call. The failure points at the finder, not at the host, which is what makes it expensive to debug. Drive every variation (text direction, a showBack flag, a locale) from notifiers inside the ONE host instead of pumping a second one.

topic: asserting flutter_svg RTL mirroring in a widget test
why: Two separate traps. (1) Asserting only that the widget carries matchTextDirection/mirrorInRtl passes even if the renderer ignores it - it proves the flag, not the picture. (2) flutter_svg puts the mirroring Transform INSIDE the SvgPicture subtree (AppSvg > SvgPicture > VectorGraphic > Semantics > SizedBox > FittedBox > SizedBox > Transform > _RawPictureVectorGraphicWidget), so it is a descendant, never an ancestor - find.ancestor silently matches nothing and the test reads as "not mirrored". It also only exists once the SVG has decoded, which happens off the main isolate, so pumping fake durations alone is not enough; runAsync has to let real time elapse first. Verified in vector_graphics-1.2.3/lib/src/vector_graphics.dart:492, which wraps the picture in Transform(Matrix4.identity()..translate(width)..scale(-1, 1)) when Directionality.of(context) is RTL.

topic: non-flex Text beside an Expanded sibling in a Row overflows
why:
In a Row, Flutter lays out non-flex children first with unbounded main-axis constraints, then divides what is LEFT among the flex children. So a bare Text takes its full intrinsic width and `maxLines` + `TextOverflow.ellipsis` never fire — there is no bound to ellipse against — and the row overflows instead. An Expanded sibling does not rescue it; it only shrinks itself.

Found concretely: `RenderFlex overflowed by 7.0 pixels` in Arabic and `by 84 pixels` in English on the order card, where "تاريخ الزيارة المؤكد" sits opposite "السبت ١٢ سبتمبر ٢٠٢٦". It stayed latent for months and only surfaced when a localization key got longer — the status badge went from 4 short group names ("جديد"/"نشط") to the backend's 13 real state names ("بانتظار استكمال العقد").

Two lasting rules:
1. `maxLines` + `overflow` on a Text is only half the guard. The Text also needs a bounded width: `Flexible`/`Expanded` inside a Row, or an explicit `BoxConstraints(maxWidth:)` when it is handed to a parent as a slot (`trailing`, `leading`) whose layout you do not control.
2. Translated strings are not fixed-width. Verify a row with the LONGEST key in BOTH ar and en before shipping — en often runs ~2x the Arabic pixel width for the same meaning, which is why the same row overflowed by 7px in one locale and 84px in the other. Shortening the English copy is a legitimate half of the fix, but only alongside the layout bound.

A doc comment claiming flexible behaviour ("Loose, so a short label still takes only the width it needs") is not the behaviour — this row carried exactly that comment above a non-flex Text. Read the widget, not the comment.

topic: building a launch Uri from a backend free-text value
why:
`Uri.tryParse` almost never returns null and `host.isEmpty` is not a validity check — percent-encoding makes junk like "coop 4" parse with a non-empty host. A model getter that turns a server value into a launchable Uri must return null for anything that is not actually launchable, because null is what the navigation layer turns into the "couldn't open this" toast. A bogus Uri instead produces a silent dead end: launchUrl reports success and the customer lands on a browser error.

Two further points this getter settles, both from reading the payload rather than guessing:
- `whatsapp` sends a bare number (`+963944123456`), so it must become `https://wa.me/<digits>`; a `tel:` opens the dialer instead of the chat.
- `phone` keeps the leading `+` when stripping formatting — it is what makes the number dialable from abroad.

Caught by a unit test, not by the analyzer. Any getter mapping untrusted backend text to a Uri deserves one.

topic: context.translate needs its own import in screens
why: `context.translate` lives in `core/localization/context_translate.dart` as a BuildContext extension, and `Failure.text(context)` lives in `failure_localizer.dart`. A screen that already shows failure toasts has the second import but not the first, so adding the first plain translated string to it fails `flutter analyze` with undefined_method. Whenever a new `context.translate(...)` call is added to a file, check that `context_translate.dart` is imported in that same file.

topic: nullable constructor param with a non-null fallback field
why:
Two separate analyzer complaints with one root cause: wanting a public named param to fall back to another value.

1. `: _sentTo = sentTo` trips `prefer_initializing_formals`, and the private-field-plus-getter dance exists only to supply a default. Dart puts initializing formals in scope inside the initializer list as parameters, so `sentTo ?? identifier` is legal there and `??` is const-safe — the constructor stays `const`. The field becomes non-null, which removes the getter and every `?.` downstream.

2. Declaring `final double? trailingGap;` while the parameter is a plain `double? trailingGap` is a hard error (`final_not_initialized_constructor`), not a lint — nothing ever assigns it. Write `this.trailingGap`.

Pick by when the default is known: fixed at construction (an args object) → resolve in the initializer list and make the field non-null; depends on build-time state or another live field → nullable field via `this.`, resolved with `??` at the use site.
